reads.sell: Albariño from the Atlantic coast of Galicia: white peach, lime and a breath of sea salt, crisp and bone dry with no oak at all. It is made for the raw bar, so think oysters, grilled prawns or octopus.

why.grape: White peach and citrus wrapped in a saline, wet stone finish with racy acid, a pithy, faintly bitter grip and no oak point to Albariño, saltier than Pinot Grigio and without the green grassiness of Sauvignon Blanc.
why.climate: High acidity, moderate alcohol and fruit poised between tart and just ripe say a cool, wet Atlantic site.
